summary: Control-plane residency propagation delay causing auth retries and mixed-egress paths
description:
Issue summary: Customer (Acme Analytics, dedicated) reports intermittent 500/502-like behavior and large p99 latency spikes for requests pinned to us-west after toggling residency enforcement. Impact: client-visible P99 increased from ~220ms to spikes around 3s for ~2-3 minute windows. Multiple tenants in same AZ observed transient auth retries and mixed egress (some requests routed to us-east).

Observed behavior: After a control-plane residency policy update (manual strict toggle by operations), edge proxies and gateway caches briefly routed a subset of traffic to the secondary region. During that window, downstream auth header validation failed intermittently causing 401->retry cycles and subsequent longer tail latencies. Expected behavior: control-plane residency change should propagate without creating mixed-egress routing for pinned sessions; auth headers should be accepted or a deterministic failover path used.

Impact: P1 customer experiencing degraded inference latency and some failed requests affecting a production job pipeline. This reduces confidence in residency toggles during business hours.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In dedicated control plane, toggle residency enforcement from 'preferred' to 'strict' for tenant acme-analytics (scheduled change performed at 02:12 UTC).
2) Observe control-plane API logs for policy broadcast: POST /v1/residency/policies -> 200
3) Monitor edge-proxy logs in us-west (edge-*-prod) and routing table snapshots for 2 minutes following the change
4) Replay a client workload that pins region via request header 'X-Region-Pin: us-west' at ~150 RPS for 5 minutes
5) Observe intermittent 401 auth failures, gateway retries, and routing to us-east for ~5-10% of requests during a 1-3 minute window.
logs: [2026-03-10T02:12:03Z] control-plane: broadcast policy id=pol-87d2 ttl=60s -> queued to edge-proxies
[2026-03-10T02:12:05Z] edge-proxy(us-west-1): cache miss policy pol-87d2; fetching from control-plane
[2026-03-10T02:12:06Z] edge-proxy(us-west-1): auth-check failed (token-stale) user=svc-acme request_id=8a3f... -> returning 401
[2026-03-10T02:12:06Z] gateway: retrying request_id=8a3f... -> routed to us-east-edge-2 due to policy fallback
comments: Asha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer reported large P99 tail after we flipped residency enforcement. Provided initial metrics and asked for SRE help. Linked dashboards: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/acme/residency-toggle?from=now-1h

Diego Martinez (SRE) - 2026-03-10: I see a short window where edge-proxy TTLs didn't invalidate synchronously. Hypothesis: control-plane published new policy before some edges refreshed auth cache, allowing mixed routing. Investigating stash sync and auth-token TTL alignment.

Kara Li (Platform) - 2026-03-11: Noted that control-plane broadcast path recently had a change to increase parallelism; could cause out-of-order propagation under load. Added a temporary guard to serialize broadcasts for residency updates. Will run canary.
Customer (Acme Analytics) - 2026-03-11: Impacting nightly batch jobs; would like an explanation and mitigation steps. Asking if we can annotate future toggles with a maintenance window.

Diego Martinez (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Applied hotfix to control-plane to sequence policy broadcasts and reduced edge cache TTLs for residency keys from 60s to 15s for the canary group. Monitoring for reoccurrence.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Control-plane broadcast happens, but edge-proxy policy cache uses async refresh leading to stale policy window. Evidence: control-plane shows broadcast at 02:12:03Z but some edges still logged cache hits for old policy at 02:12:05Z.

Hypothesis 2: Auth token validation TTL mismatch - tokens issued while policy changed lacked new audience claim; edges rejected then retried which triggered failover. Evidence: 401 messages include 'token-stale' and token issuance time ~02:11:59Z.

Metric notes: us-west p95 jump from 220ms -> 1.2s, p99 up to ~3.4s for 2.5 minutes. Retry rate increased from 0.2% -> 6% during window. Errors correlated with requests that were retried and routed to us-east.
Control-plane PRs correlating with change: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4281 (changed broadcast parallelism, merged 2026-03-09)

Edge config: residency cache TTL default 60s; auth token acceptance grace window 5s. Mismatch causes small window where new residency policy is in effect but edge's auth cache rejects tokens from its local validator.
Reproduction attempts in staging with same load showed same pattern when broadcasts were parallelized. Serializing broadcasts removed mixed-egress in test runs.
Temporary mitigation: serialized broadcasts and reduced residency TTL on canary edges. Longer-term fix: introduce ordered broadcast acknowledgement + atomic policy application around auth validators.
resolution: Mitigation applied: control-plane broadcast serialization added (hotfix), residency cache TTL reduced for canary edges, and auth validator grace window increased to absorb transient policy handovers. Customer notified and observed no recurrence during 24h post-fix. Next steps: schedule a formal rollout of broadcast serialization, add monitoring alert for 'residency-toggle-mixed-egress' and iterate on runbook. Follow-up ticket created for full rollout: SUP-740002.
postmortem_action_items: 1) Full rollout of broadcast serialization to all control-plane instances (owner: Platform) - due 2026-03-18
2) Align default residency cache TTL and auth token grace window (owner: Auth team) - due 2026-03-20
3) Add an SLO alert for >1% retry-rate spike following residency policy changes (owner: SRE) - due 2026-03-15
4) Update maintenance guidance for customers performing residency toggles and offer scheduled windows for Enterprise/Dedicated tenants (owner: CS) - due 2026-03-22
